pi_r_definition:
pi_r(v_r) is the Lebesgue density (with respect to Euclidean volume on R^(2d+2), orthonormal gradient coordinates, ST 84-86 and 226-229) of the transformed row vector U_r F of equation (6), evaluated at the exact target v_r of (7). It is defined from the original two-site observation density p_O through the invertible linear transform, ST 206-207 (8): p_O(b,0,b-k r^3,0)=12 r^(-(d+3)) pi_r(v_r), and the version used is fixed by COUNT: ST 110-113 "All contact density and conditional-law versions below are induced from these same specified COUNT versions by the invertible observation transform, rather than chosen independently on exceptional fibers." ST 392-394 ledger entry: "original observation density 12 r^(-(d+3)) pi_r(v_r)".

Its r->0 limit pi_0(v_0) (CONTACT row, ST line 45: "For literal rows/targets in Section 3, pi_r(v_r) converges to pi_0(v_0)") is the density of the contact jet vector U_0=(F,F_u,F_uu,F_uuu,(F_vi,F_uvi)_(i=1..d-1)) (ST 215) at v_0=(b,0,0,12k,(0,0)_i) (ST 216). Coordinates that survive in the limit observation: the height F (pinned at b), the full gradient grad F=(F_u,F_v1..F_v(d-1)) (pinned at 0), the full axial Hessian column V=Hess F(u,.)=(F_uu,F_uv1,...,F_uv(d-1)) (pinned at 0), and the single third derivative F_uuu (pinned at 12k). The transverse Hessian block A=Hess F|_(u-perp) is NOT part of the observation; it enters only through the weight (see W_r). ST 456-459 names these: "odd: G=grad F (dimension d), T=F_uuu (one scalar); even: F, V=Hess F(u,.) (dimension d), A=Hess F|_(u-perp). (15) Here V=(F_uu,F_uv_1,...,F_uv_(d-1)). It is the full axial column, not the single entry F_uu."

Under the additional centered-Gaussian parity contract (ST 452-457), ST 475: "pi_0(v_0)=p_(F,V)(b,0) p_G(0) phi_tau(12k)", with tau_(x,u)^2=Var(T|G=0)>0 (ST 469, equation (16)).

SG proves the convergence for the Gaussian field: SG 336-348: "Let Sigma_r=Cov(U_r), and let c_r=E[F U_r F] ... Sigma_r->Sigma_0 uniformly, ||c_r-c_0||C4<=Cr E||F||C4^2. (15) ... Rank (9) and compactness of O(d) give Sigma_0>=lambda I, and then Sigma_r>=lambda I/2 for a common small r_0>0. Upper covariance bounds also hold. Density pi_r(v_r) therefore converges at every fixed b,k,u to pi_0(v_0)." Here pi_r is the centered Gaussian density of U_r F with covariance Sigma_r, evaluated at v_r.
W_r_and_sigma:
W (typed determinant weight), ST Section 2, lines 78-81, equation (2):
    O_(p,q)=(F(p),grad F(p),F(q),grad F(q)),
    Delta_(p,q)=|det Hess F(p) det Hess F(q)|,
    tau_(p,q)=1{Hess F(p)<0} 1{Hess F(q) has index d-1},
    W_(p,q)=Delta_(p,q) tau_(p,q).                           (2)
ST 83-84: "The index indicator is restricted to nonsingular Hessians. A change on a singular Hessian has no effect because its determinant is zero." ST 96-97: applying (3) to w=tau sigma 1{F(p)-F(q) in I} "gives W sigma. Delta appears exactly once." W_r is W_(M,S) at the contact pair M=exp_x(-ru/2), S=exp_x(ru/2) (ST 175); SG 376: "with W_r the actual typed determinant product".

Q_r (conditional law): ST 98-100: "Disintegrating the two heights with actual density p_O and an actual regular conditional field kernel Q^p,q_(b,s) gives K_sel(p,q,b,s)=p_O(b,0,s,0) E_Q[W_(p,q) sigma(p,q,F)]" (equation (4), lines 100-102). Q^{p,q}_(b,s) is the regular conditional law of the whole field given O_(p,q)=(b,0,s,0). ST 104: "Joint Borel versions of p_O and Q are part of COUNT." Q_r is this kernel at (p,q)=(M,S), s=b-k r^3, i.e. given U_r F=v_r (equivalently O=(b,0,b-kr^3,0) by invertibility, ST 110-113); Q_0 is the limiting conditional law given U_0 F=v_0. ST 106-108: "A conditional kernel can be singular in unused second-jet coordinates. Full two-site Hessian rank is not required." ST 331-333 (random-law adapter): "suppose the specified Q_r and Q_0 can be coupled with global C4 convergence, exact pins and an integrable dominating variable for V_r at each fixed mark." SG's concrete Q_r, lines 350-357, equation (16): "F_r=F+c_r Sigma_r^(-1)(v_r-U_r F). (16) This satisfies its pins exactly. Its centered residual is independent of U_r F by Gaussian orthogonality on a dense evaluation set. Thus it is the canonical full-field conditional law Q_r, including at null pin events." SG 359 (17): ||F_r||C4<=C||F||C4+C(|b|+k).

SG 296-297 reuses it: "The intrinsic rational-superlevel connectivity selector of ST is Borel on C4 fields and zero outside the open Morse/distinct locus."

ST 263, equation (12): "V_r:=W_r/r^2 -> V_0:=36k^2 (det A_0)^2 1{A_0<0}." ST 381: "Write z_0(b,k,x,u)=E_Q0 V_0". ST 476 (parity form): "z_0=36k^2 E[(det A)^2 1{A<0} | F=b,V=0]." SG 378-379 (18): "V_r=W_r/r^2 -> V_0=36k^2(det A_0)^2 1{A_0<0}, V_r<=C(1+||F_r||C3)^(2d)." SG 385-386: "Thus z_0=E V_0 is positive and finite at every fixed b in R,k>0 and E_Qr V_r->z_0."

Where the pieces come from (ST 233-263): under the exact pins the physical Hessians are H_i=[r alpha_i, r beta_i^T; r beta_i, A_i] (ST 236-237, (10)), A_i the physical transverse Hessian block at i=M,S (ST 233); ST 244-245: "alpha_M -> -6k, alpha_S -> 6k, beta_M,beta_S bounded, A_M,A_S -> A_0"; ST 247-248: "the first limit follows from integrating F_uu along the geodesic, whose average is zero, and whose derivative tends to F_uuu=12k"; ST 253 (11): "det H_i/r=alpha_i det A_i-r beta_i^T adj(A_i) beta_i"; ST 255: "For d=1 use det A=1 and omit the second term."

Classification of the quantities (as the documents define them; no analysis of F here): Hessian-type quantities are Delta=|det Hess F(M) det Hess F(S)| (two d-by-d Hessian determinants, ST 79), the blocks alpha_i (scalar axial Hessian entry), beta_i (d-1 vector of mixed Hessian entries) and A_i (the (d-1)-by-(d-1) transverse Hessian block) in (10), their limits alpha_M=-6k, alpha_S=6k (ST 244, which are Hessian entries whose values are fixed by the third-derivative pin 12k), A_0, det A_0 (one (d-1)-by-(d-1) determinant, squared in V_0), the type indicators tau (ST 80) and 1{A_0<0} (ST 263), and the axial column V=Hess F(u,.) and the even block A in (15) (ST 456-457). Heights: b, b-k r^3, b-k r^3/2 (first row of v_r), (ST 191-193). Gradients: g_uM,g_uS,g_iM,g_iS pinned to zero, G=grad F in (15), the row (h_S-h_M)/r with target -k r^2 which tends to F_u=0. Third derivative: the fourth row (6/r^2)[...] with target 12k, tending to T=F_uuu=12k (ST 188, 193, 215-216, 248, 456). The factor 36k^2 in V_0 is the product (-6k)(6k) squared in absolute value, i.e. alpha_M alpha_S with alpha_i->+-6k, from ST 244 and (11).

far_definition:
FAR contract, ST line 48: "The complement integral in the specified kernel representative (4) is a finite, locally integrable Borel lifetime density nu_far, with ell^(1/3) nu_far(ell)->0. A uniform O(1) far candidate bound is sufficient." Falsifier: "A remote small-lifetime contribution of comparable or larger order."

The representative (4), ST 100-102:
    K_sel(p,q,b,s)=p_O(b,0,s,0) E_Q[W_(p,q) sigma(p,q,F)],
    nu_bar(ell)=V_X^(-1) integral_(p!=q) integral_R K_sel(p,q,b,b-ell) db dvol(p) dvol(q).   (4)
ST 113-114: "FAR likewise refers to the complement of (4) itself. This fixes the representative for the pointwise conclusion." The near part is the portion of (4) with dist(p,q)=r<=r_0 (ST 354, 407-417, with the indicator 1{k>=ell/r_0^3} in the near integral); nu_far is the remaining part of (4), i.e. pairs with dist(p,q)>r_0. ST 429-431: "FAR supplies the entire remaining finite-bar contribution, because COUNT already counts all bars once. Its scaled limit is zero. Hence ell^(1/3) nu_bar(ell)->C."

SG version, lines 304-306 (SG equation (12), the torus form of ST (4)): "K_sel(p,q,b,s)=p_O(b,0,s,0) E_Q[W_(p,q) sigma], nu_bar(ell)=L^(-d) integral_(p!=q) integral_R K_sel(p,q,b,b-ell) db dp dq. (12)". SG Section 7, lines 473-484: "For dist(p,q)>=r_0, the original O_(p,q) covariance has a positive floor by (9), continuity and compactness. Conditional regression at target (b,0,b-ell,0), 0<ell<=1, gives a C2-norm moment polynomial in |b| and a Gaussian observation density bounded by C exp(-c b^2). Integrating the determinant product over b and the compact pair domain gives 0<=nu_bar,far(ell)<=nu_cand,far(ell)<=C. (22) Any fixed compact positive-lifetime band similarly has a finite local bound. This is a direct density bound for the representative (12), not differentiation of a cumulative estimate. It proves FAR." SG 509-510: "the far term vanishes after multiplication by ell^(1/3)." (SG (4), lines 57-58, is the conclusion nu_bar(ell) ~ c_q ell^(-1/3), E N_t/L^d ~ (3/2) c_q t^(2/3), not the far object; the "kernel representative (4)" named in ST's FAR row is ST's (4) at lines 100-102.)

Yes. In the Gaussian/parity case the limit density pi_0(v_0) contains a Gaussian density factor evaluated at the fourth-coordinate target 12k, i.e. the third-derivative pin F_uuu=12k.

SG: the finite-r fourth row and its kernel, SG 317-321 (13): fourth row "(6/r^2)[F_u(M)+F_u(S)-2(F(S)-F(M))/r]", target "12k". Its kernel has mass one. All other rows are averages/divided differences of derivatives of order at most two." Combining the exact 12 factor in (24) yields" SG 540-543 (27): "c_q=Gamma(7/6)/(24^(1/3)sqrt(pi)) *integral_S p_G(0) p_Vu(0) tau_u^(4/3) D_u d sigma(u), p_G(0)=(2pi)^(-d/2)(det M_G)^(-1/2), p_Vu(0)=(2pi)^(-d/2)(det M_Vu)^(-1/2)."

In the general (non-parity) structural statement the k-dependence of the limit integrand in ST (14) (lines 425-427) enters through pi_0(v_0) = density of U_0 at v_0=(b,0,0,12k,0...) Notation. A = aR has density p_A(s) = alpha a^(-alpha) s^(alpha-1) on (0,a), a = sqrt((alpha+2)/alpha), independent of the Gaussian field H (AMP (6)). Conditional on A = s, F = sH. For a bar of H with marks (b_H,k_H,ell_H,x,u) the F-bar has (s b_H, s k_H, s ell_H, x, u), same critical points and elder pairing (AMP (8), lines 134-143).

Derivation of the exponent from the ledger (ST 390-400, SG 486-493), entry by entry, conditional on A = s:
(i) Observation. O^F_(p,q) = (F(p),grad F(p),F(q),grad F(q)) = s O^H_(p,q), a vector of dimension 2d+2 (ST 78, 195). Hence p^F_O(o | A=s) = s^(-(2d+2)) p^H_O(o/s). The transform O -> U_r of ST (6) is linear, so U_r F = s U_r H and the Jacobian 12 r^(-(d+3)) of ST (8) is unchanged (r is the same physical separation). Therefore pi^F_r(v | A=s) = s^(-(2d+2)) pi^H_r(v/s). The target v_r(b,k) = (b-k r^3/2, -k r^2, 0, 12k, 0...) of ST (7) is homogeneous of degree one in (b,k): v_r(b,k)/s = v_r(b/s,k/s). So pi^F_r(v_r(b,k) | A=s) = s^(-(2d+2)) pi^H_r(v_r(b/s,k/s)).
(ii) Conditional law. Q^F_r(b,k | A=s) = (S_s)_# Q^H_r(b/s,k/s), where S_s is multiplication by s (the law of sH given s U_r H = v_r(b,k), i.e. U_r H = v_r(b/s,k/s)).
(iii) Typed determinant weight. Hess F = s Hess H, so det Hess F(p) = s^d det Hess H(p), Delta^F = s^(2d) Delta^H (two d-by-d determinants, ST (2)); the type indicator tau is invariant under s>0 (definiteness and index are scale invariant). Thus W^F_r = s^(2d) W^H_r and V^F_r = W^F_r/r^2 = s^(2d) V^H_r (r unchanged). Also sigma(sH) = sigma(H): the Morse/distinct set G is scale invariant, critical points and their indices are the same, and D_(sH)(p) = s D_H(p) because the condition in ST (5) is monotone in lambda (a down-set), so its supremum over Q equals the supremum over the dense set s^(-1)Q; hence D_(sH)(p) = sH(q) iff D_H(p) = H(q).
(iv) Product. For any bounded nonnegative g in {1, sigma, 1-sigma}, pi^F_r(v_r(b,k)) E_(Q^F_r)[V^F_r g] = integral p_A(s) s^(-(2d+2)) pi^H_r(v_r(b/s,k/s)) s^(2d) E_(Q^H_r(b/s,k/s))[V^H_r g] ds = E[ A^(-2) (pi^H_r E_(Q^H_r)[V^H_r g])(b/A, k/A) ].
(Here Q^F_r(b,k) is the Bayes mixture: posterior on A with density proportional to p_A(s) s^(-(2d+2)) pi^H_r(v_r(b/s,k/s)), then (S_s)_# Q^H_r(b/s,k/s); it is normalizable for every k>0 because |v_r(b/s,k/s)|^2 >= 144 k^2/s^2 and pi^H_r(v) <= C exp(-c|v|^2) uniformly for 0<r<=r_0 by SG 346-347, so s^(-(2d+2)) pi^H_r(...) <= C s^(-(2d+2)) exp(-c k^2/s^2) is bounded on (0,a).)
Hence the exact identity, for all 0<r<=r_0, all (b,k), k>0, all alpha>0:
    B^F_r(b,k) = E[ A^(-2) B^H_r(b/A, k/A) ],   B_r = 12 pi_r(v_r) E_(Q_r)[V_r sigma],
and the same with the unselected product (g = 1) and with the failure term (g = 1-sigma). The exponent q = 2 = (2d+2) - 2d: the observation density of dimension 2d+2 contributes A^(-(2d+2)), the two Hessian determinants contribute A^(+2d); r^(d-1) dr, 12 r^(-(d+3)) and r^2 are unchanged because r is physical. Equivalently, q = 2 is the dimension of the scaled mark pair (b,k): the ledger line r B_r dr db dk with db dk = A^2 db' dk' shows that the F near-ledger at (b',k',r) in H-coordinates has exactly the mass of the H ledger (bars are in bijection), which is the ST 390-400 cancellation restated for the mixture. The mixture also reproduces AMP (9): nu_F(ell) = E[A^(-1) nu_H(ell/A)] (one extra factor A from db = A db').
The same identity holds on the far fibers: K^F_sel(p,q,b,s) = E[A^(-2) K^H_sel(p,q,b/A,s/A)] for dist(p,q) > r_0, giving nu_(F,far)(ell) = E[A^(-1) nu_(H,far)(ell/A)].

(a) A>0 a.s. and F = AH, so F is C4 with the same critical points, indices and ordering of critical values as H (AMP 134-143); H is Morse/distinct a.s. (SG Section 4), hence so is F for every alpha. Height laws are non-atomic (mixture of Gaussians by a positive amplitude), so the COUNT falsifier 'atomic height laws' is absent. (b) The selector of ST (5), 136-141 is Borel on C4 fields (ST 144, SG 296-297) and sigma(sH) = sigma(H) (monotonicity of the chain condition in lambda gives D_(sH) = s D_H; G is scale invariant); it counts each finite bar of F once because the bars of F are the bars of H with scaled heights (AMP (8)). (c) Formula (3) for F: condition on A = s. For fixed s, sH is a C4 Gaussian field with the same rank structure, so SG (11) applies: E sum_(p!=q) w(p,q,sH) = integral p^(sH)_grad(0) E[Delta^(sH) w | grads=0] = integral p^H_grad(0) E_H[Delta^H w(p,q,sH) | grad H = 0] dp dq, because the density factor s^(-2d) and the determinant factor s^(2d) cancel. Integrating in s by Tonelli (nonnegative w) gives E sum w(p,q,F) = integral rho_w(p,q) dp dq with rho_w = E_A[p^H_grad(0) E_H[Delta^H w(.,AH) | grad H=0]] finite. For g != 0 the F gradient density p^F_grad(g) = E[A^(-2d) p^H_grad(g/A)] is finite (Gaussian decay exp(-c|g|^2/A^2) by the gradient covariance floor) and the Bayes conditional law Q^F_g is a normalizable mixture; the weighted density p^F_grad(g) E_(Q^F_g)[Delta^F w] = E_A[p^H_grad(g/A) E_H[Delta^H w(AH)|g/A]] is continuous in g with value rho_w at g = 0. So (3) holds for F with this specified version of the product. Caveat: p^F_grad(0) = E[A^(-2d)] p^H_grad(0) = +infinity iff alpha <= 2d (integral_0^a s^(alpha-1-2d) ds diverges), and then the Bayes posterior at the exact fiber g = 0 is not normalizable (proportional to s^(alpha-1-2d)); the product in (3) must be read as the Radon-Nikodym density rho_w of the Delta-weighted gradient measure at 0 ('extended nonnegative integral ... specified versions', ST 88-94, 104), not as a finite density times a conditional expectation. This is a null fiber of the gradient-only disintegration and does not affect (4). (d) Two-height disintegration (4): on every fiber (b,0,s,0) with s != b (lifetime ell = b-s > 0), p^F_O(b,0,s,0) = E[A^(-(2d+2)) p^H_O((b,0,s,0)/A)] is finite for every alpha, because |o|^2 = b^2+s^2 >= ell^2/2 and p^H_O(o) <= C exp(-c|o|^2) for dist(p,q) >= r_0 (SG 473-476), while for near pairs p^H_O = 12 r^(-(d+3)) pi^H_r(v_r) with |v_r|^2 >= 144 k^2 = 144 ell^2/r^6 (SG 346-347), so the A-integrand is bounded by C A^(-(2d+2)) exp(-c ell^2/A^2) (bounded on (0,a)). The Bayes posterior on A is normalizable on these fibers and Q^F_(b,s) = mixture of (S_A)_# Q^H_(b/A,s/A); the kernel K^F_sel(p,q,b,s) = p^F_O E_(Q^F)[W^F sigma] = E[A^(-2) K^H_sel(p,q,b/A,s/A)] is a finite Borel kernel and (4) gives nu^F_bar(ell) = E[A^(-1) nu^H_bar(ell/A)] = AMP (9) for all ell > 0, by Tonelli. The ell = 0 fiber is Lebesgue-null and not used. Hence COUNT holds for every alpha > 0 with these versions; no falsifier of ST line 44 (atomic heights, candidate counting, double determinant, failed once-counting) occurs.
